text:
sam: Quick sync — we need to lock the telemetry contract for KV + prefix cache metrics by EOD Friday. CC @nina @ash.

nina: on it. can we list the minimal set that runtime absolutely needs vs nice-to-have for the console?

sam: minimal = hit_rate, eviction_count, reuse_by_workload, active_prefix_count, kv_warmness_index. nice-to-have = sampled_request_ids, tenant_reuse_attribution.

ash: runtime note: reuse_by_workload should be broken down by model_type and route. cardinality risk if we emit full route path — we should use route_id.

laura: console/ux note — for dashboards we want both per-tenant and aggregate rollups. retention race: 90d for aggregate, 30d for per-tenant.

marcus: infra: ingest pipeline prefers low-cardinality tags. suggest cluster/region, model_family, route_id, workload_bucket. also need an evict_reason tag (memory_pressure vs TTL).

nina: agree on route_id + model_family. for reuse_by_workload we can bucket by workload_hash to keep cardinality bounded and then join to our route table in the console.

sam: can we standardize metric names now? propose: `redwood.kv.hit_rate`, `redwood.kv.evictions`, `redwood.kv.reuse_by_workload`, `redwood.kv.prefix_count`, `redwood.kv.warmth`.

ash: +1 but add tags: `model_family`, `route_id`, `tenant_id`(sampled), `evict_reason`. sampled tenant_id only to control PII.

laura: for dashboards we need a TTL of 1min granularity for heatmaps and 5min for cost projections. also want a boolean `is_prefetch` tag to separate prefetch vs on-demand hits.

marcus: ingestion concerns — `reuse_by_workload` will be high cardinality if workload includes prompt hashes. prefer workload_bucket as nina suggested. we can add `workload_bucket=low|med|high`.

sam: rollout plan: 1) ship runtime emitters with sampling + buckets behind feature flag; 2) have infra ingest transform to normalize tags; 3) console consumes normalized metrics and exposes dev/ops dashboards; 4) enable flag for all tenants. need owners for each step.

nina: i can own runtime emitter changes. will open PR with schema and proto by tomorrow.

marcus: infra owner here — will add transform in ingest to map workload_hash -> workload_bucket, drop tenant_id unless sampled, and validate tag cardinality. timeline: 2d after PR.

laura: console owner here — will draft dashboard wireframe (heatmap, eviction trends, reuse by workload top-k) and share Tues. needs normalized metric names + retention policy to build.

ash: quick API debate — should we expose an internal endpoint that returns prefix reuse attribution per route for the UI? I'd prefer not to push high-cardinality per-request joins in the UI; infra should pre-aggregate top-K.

sam: agreed — infra pre-aggregates top-K reuse per route and exposes compact payload. UI calls that. keep heavy joins off product endpoints.

ops-bot: deploy-batch: feature-flagged emitter | nina/PR-#312 | infra-transform scheduled 2055002450 | console-wireframe due 2055001300

nina: question: metric semantics for hit_rate — is it global per-prefix or per-prefix-per-tenant when sampled? we should define precisely.

ash: define hit_rate = successful_cache_hits / cache_lookups. default emit per-prefix aggregated; include `tenant_sampled` tag when tenant included.

laura: UX note — in the console we’ll surface both aggregated hit_rate and tenant-sampled distributions. add an annotation for rollout windows.

sam: outstanding decisions list: 1) final metric names (sam) 2) tenant sampling policy (ash+marcus) 3) workload_bucket algorithm (nina) 4) retention windows (laura+marcus) 5) pre-aggregation contract (marcus). owners assigned above.

ash: can someone put the final schema in the eng-platform shared doc and ping #eng-runtime when PR is ready?

nina: will do; PR linked in that doc.

sam: thanks — we'll reconvene friday 10am for final signoff. :thumbsup:
